title: The Farm Worker Whose Breath Grew Shorter Over a Year — Heart Failure, Grief, and Forty Years of Drinking

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 60 years old, presenting with a year-long history of progressively worsening breathlessness. It began as exertional, brought on by his farm work and his job as an office attendant, and eased with rest, but has now advanced to the point of incapacitating him at NYHA Grade 3. He has had no palpitations, fainting or near-fainting spells, cold sweats, or cold hands, though he does feel drowsy after meals. He has also had nocturia for the past three months.

For the past month he has had a cough with a small amount of whitish, mucoid sputum, occurring in spoonful amounts without froth or blood, along with a low-grade fever. He has also had low back pain for a month, without early-morning stiffness, persistent and only mildly relieved by rest, with no loss of appetite or weight loss.

He had an appendectomy 20 years ago. He currently takes furosemide, pantoprazole, and torsemide. He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes two months ago and is not hypertensive.

His sleep has been poor — he wakes frequently to urinate, feels drowsy during the day, and snores. He has been drinking 90–180 ml of Imperial Blue whiskey daily for nearly 40 years, which he attributes to the stress of raising eight children and to the recent death of his wife two months ago. His bowel habits are otherwise normal, though he has to strain.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General exam:** conscious, coherent, cooperative, moderately built and nourished; blood pressure 150/80 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, respiratory rate 20/min, afebrile; no pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, koilonychia, or generalized lymphadenopathy; bilateral pitting pedal edema present
- **Cardiovascular exam:** elevated jugular venous pressure and a left parasternal heave on inspection; apical impulse in the 5th intercostal space lateral to the midclavicular line, with a palpable A2 in the left 2nd intercostal space; a pansystolic murmur on auscultation with normal S1 and S2
- **Abdominal exam:** soft, distended abdomen with a slit-like umbilicus, flank fullness, a cough impulse at the umbilical region, an appendectomy scar in the right iliac fossa, rectus divarication, and visible epigastric aortic pulsations; waist circumference 91 cm, hip circumference 94 cm; liver palpable with a span of 17 cm; shifting dullness present; bowel sounds normal
- **Respiratory and neurological exam:** normal vesicular breath sounds with bilateral air entry and no added sounds; no focal neurological deficit
- **Liver function:** total bilirubin 1.02 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 0.30 mg/dL, AST 22 IU/L, ALT 16 IU/L, ALP 167 IU/L, total protein 5.9 g/dL, albumin 3.8 g/dL, A/G ratio 1.81
- **Electrolytes and renal function:** sodium 136 mEq/L, potassium 4.3 mEq/L, chloride 97 mEq/L, serum creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, fasting blood sugar 119 mg/dL
- **Imaging and cardiac work-up:** abdominal ultrasound, chest X-ray, ECG, and 2D echocardiogram were performed but findings were not detailed in the record

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content: Taking together his year-long progressive dyspnea now at NYHA Class 3, elevated JVP, parasternal heave, pansystolic murmur, pitting edema, and hepatomegaly with shifting dullness, the working diagnosis was heart failure with preserved ejection fraction associated with coronary artery disease, with pulmonary tuberculosis also considered given his month-long cough, mucoid expectoration, and low-grade fever. He was started on furosemide and B-complex supplementation, with close monitoring of his blood pressure and pulse.
